newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to present BSE food safety plans.
newsitem.headline: EU to present BSE food safety plans.

text.p: The European Commission will publish proposals for a new food safety unit next month, spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said on Thursday.

Commission President Jacques Santer told the parliament's committee of inquiry into the Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) crisis on Wednesday that he planned to separate management of food safety and farm policy.
"All Commissioners at today's meeting supported the president's general line on BSE," van der Pas said after the Commissioners' weekly meeting, adding that details would be ready before February 19.

The proposals for reorganisation are an internal issue but will include budgetary implications which will be part of the annual budgetary process and other areas where the Commission cannot act alone, he said.

The planned changes follow an internal Commission inquiry into the handling of the mad cow crisis which had prompted the view that food safety should be under one Commissioner rather than several at now.
The mad cow crisis flared up in March 1996 after Britain, where BSE is most widespread, announced that the fatal cattle brain disease could be transmitted to people who ate infected beef.
